justification:
ING. JABESH AMISSAH-ARTHUR

Introduction

Ing. Jabesh Amissah-Arthur is a distinguished Ghanaian engineer, energy executive and public-sector leader whose career spans more than four decades of dedicated service to Ghana and the wider West African region.

His career represents an exceptional combination of technical excellence, public-sector leadership, institutional development, policy contribution, infrastructure delivery and commitment to national development. From pioneering information technology applications at the Volta River Authority (VRA) in the 1980s, to leading major national electrification initiatives, serving as Deputy Chief Executive of VRA, delivering the 400 MW Bui Hydroelectric Project and authoring Ghana’s National Electricity Grid Code, he has consistently placed his expertise at the service of the nation.

He has held several influential leadership positions, including Deputy Chief Executive of the Volta River Authority, Chief Executive Officer of the Bui Power Authority and Board Chair of the Volta River Authority. He has also served in significant regional and national leadership capacities, contributing to energy development and cooperation across West Africa.

He currently serves as the Operations Chair for the Private Sector Participation Programme, demonstrating that his commitment to national service and energy-sector governance remains active. In this capacity, he continues to bring his extensive experience, institutional knowledge and leadership to matters concerning the effective participation of the private sector in Ghana’s energy development.

His distinguished contribution to Ghana’s energy sector was formally recognised in 2025 when he was adjudged the recipient of the Lifetime Achievement Award at the Ghana Energy Awards. This recognition is an important testament to the depth and longevity of his contribution.

However, his case for the Distinguished Public Service and Governance Award rests on a much broader record: more than four decades of service in which he has helped build institutions, expand access to electricity, establish enduring governance frameworks, deliver strategic national infrastructure, develop Ghanaian professionals and contribute to regional cooperation.

Major Contributions to Public Service and Governance

1. Pioneering Innovation in the Public Sector

Ing. Amissah-Arthur’s contribution to public service began with his work at the Volta River Authority, where he demonstrated that Ghanaian professionals could successfully tackle highly complex technical challenges and introduce innovative solutions within public institutions.

In 1987, as a young engineer at VRA, he successfully migrated the Authority’s Computerised Reservoir Simulation Model from IBM mainframes onto the newly acquired WANG mainframes and desktops. The assignment had defeated a team of international consultants and computer science graduates, but Ing. Amissah-Arthur successfully delivered the solution.

This achievement demonstrated not only technical competence but also an early commitment to improving the effectiveness and efficiency of a major public institution through innovation.

Between 1990 and 1995, he became the first Ghanaian to head VRA’s Management Information Systems (MIS) Department. During this period, he developed and implemented VRA’s first IT strategy and led the institution’s transition from mainframe computing to desktop personal computers. His leadership contributed significantly to modernising the Authority’s operations and establishing systems that improved institutional efficiency.

His work is an early example of his broader public-service philosophy: public institutions must continually evolve, embrace innovation and build internal capacity to deliver effectively.

2. Leadership of the Northern Electrification and System Reinforcement Project

One of Ing. Amissah-Arthur’s most significant contributions to national development came through the Northern Electrification and System Reinforcement Project (NESRP).

He led a five-member professional team that conducted VRA’s first feasibility study for a major energy-access project. The study provided the technical and economic justification required to secure financing from the African Development Bank and the World Bank.

He was subsequently appointed Office Engineer for the project, with responsibility for supervising, coordinating and controlling its implementation.

His responsibilities covered design, contracting, finance, construction, administration, technical coordination and project reporting.

The successful completion of the project extended electricity infrastructure from Kumasi to the northern-most parts of Ghana and helped establish the backbone for the country’s National Electrification Programme.

This was more than an engineering achievement. It was a major public-service intervention that expanded access to electricity for communities that had previously been underserved.

The long-term benefits of this contribution extend across education, healthcare, agriculture, commerce, industry and household welfare.

3. Executive Leadership at the Volta River Authority

At the age of only 42, Ing. Amissah-Arthur was appointed Deputy Chief Executive of the Volta River Authority.

The appointment placed him in one of the most strategically important positions in Ghana’s energy sector, with responsibility for engineering, design, construction, operations and maintenance of the country’s generation plants and transmission networks.

He assumed this responsibility at a critical stage in Ghana’s energy development.

At the time, the country’s electricity infrastructure faced increasing demands for reliability and expansion, while the functions now associated with GRIDCo remained within VRA.

His leadership therefore required a combination of technical expertise, operational discipline, strategic planning and public accountability.

He was also responsible for electricity distribution across northern Ghana, further connecting his executive responsibilities to the broader national objective of expanding reliable electricity access.

His performance in this role demonstrated his ability to manage complex public-sector responsibilities while balancing institutional priorities with the national interest.

4. Transformational Leadership at the Bui Power Authority

Perhaps one of the clearest examples of Ing. Amissah-Arthur’s public-sector leadership was his tenure as Chief Executive Officer of the Bui Power Authority from 2009 to 2017.

Under his leadership, the Authority successfully delivered the 400 MW Bui Hydroelectric Project, one of Ghana’s most important energy infrastructure projects.

The project was delivered on schedule and within budget, representing a major achievement in project governance, financial discipline, technical coordination and institutional leadership.

However, his contribution went beyond the physical construction of the dam.

Ing. Amissah-Arthur placed strong emphasis on building Ghanaian institutional and technical capacity. He championed the use of Ghanaian professionals in the supervision, commissioning, operations and maintenance of the project.

This approach demonstrated confidence in Ghanaian expertise and created opportunities for local professionals to acquire and exercise the skills required to manage complex national infrastructure.

The Bui project therefore became not only an important addition to Ghana’s generation capacity but also an important demonstration of Ghanaian professional competence.

His leadership at Bui reflects an important principle of good public governance: major national projects should deliver both immediate infrastructure and long-term institutional capacity.

5. Author of Ghana’s National Electricity Grid Code

Ing. Amissah-Arthur’s contribution to governance extends significantly into policy and regulatory development.

He authored Ghana’s National Electricity Grid Code, which has guided the operation of the National Interconnected Transmission System since 2009.

The Grid Code established important standards governing the planning, performance, operation, reliability and security of Ghana’s electricity transmission system.

It also provides a framework for open and non-discriminatory access to the transmission network.

The continued relevance and use of the Grid Code demonstrate the enduring nature of his contribution to energy governance.

Rather than merely managing an institution during his tenure, he contributed to establishing a framework that continues to guide the sector long after his direct involvement in its creation.

This is one of the strongest indicators of his contribution to governance: he helped establish systems capable of outlasting the individuals who created them.

6. Institutional Leadership and Governance

Throughout his career, Ing. Amissah-Arthur has demonstrated a commitment to strengthening institutions rather than simply occupying leadership positions.

His leadership roles have included Deputy Chief Executive of the Volta River Authority; Chief Executive Officer of the Bui Power Authority; Board Chair of the Volta River Authority; Chief Executive Officer and Board Member of the Bui Power Authority; Chair of the West African Gas Pipeline Authority (WAGPA); Chair of the Takoradi International Company (TiCO); and Power Group Co-Chair of the Ghana–USA Partnership for Growth.

Across these roles, he has contributed to institutional decision-making, strategic planning, infrastructure development and energy-sector governance.

His leadership record reflects an understanding that strong institutions are fundamental to sustainable national development.

7. Continuing Contribution Through the Private Sector Participation Programme

Ing. Amissah-Arthur’s commitment to public service remains active.

He currently serves as the Operations Chair for the Private Sector Participation Programme, where he continues to contribute his experience and expertise to Ghana’s energy-sector development.

His current role is particularly significant because Ghana’s energy sector increasingly requires effective collaboration between government institutions and private-sector participants.

Through this role, he continues to contribute to the processes, structures and relationships required to facilitate effective private-sector participation in national energy development.

His continued service demonstrates that his contribution to Ghana has not ended with his previous executive appointments. Instead, his decades of experience continue to be deployed in support of national policy, institutional development and energy-sector governance.

This continuity is a defining feature of his career: he has consistently made himself available to serve where his expertise can contribute to Ghana’s development.

8. Regional Public Service and West African Impact

Ing. Amissah-Arthur’s contribution has also extended beyond Ghana.

He has contributed to or led more than 40 major energy-sector projects across West Africa, providing technical and strategic expertise to initiatives that support regional energy integration and development.

His regional leadership roles, including his involvement with the West African Gas Pipeline Authority, demonstrate his contribution to energy cooperation beyond Ghana’s borders.

Through these engagements, he has contributed to efforts to strengthen regional energy infrastructure, cooperation and integration.

His influence therefore extends from the national level to the wider West African energy landscape.

9. Development of Ghanaian Human Capital

A defining feature of Ing. Amissah-Arthur’s public-service legacy is his commitment to developing Ghanaian professionals.

Throughout his career, he has consistently demonstrated confidence in Ghanaian technical capacity.

His decision to empower Ghanaian professionals in the delivery, commissioning, operation and maintenance of the Bui Hydroelectric Project is one of the clearest examples.

He has also mentored and supported generations of engineers and energy professionals who have gone on to assume leadership responsibilities across Ghana’s energy sector.

His contribution is therefore not limited to the projects he personally delivered. It also lives on through the professionals whose careers were influenced by his leadership.

This is an important dimension of distinguished public service: building people who can continue serving the nation after one’s own tenure has ended.

10. Commitment to National Development

Across more than four decades, Ing. Amissah-Arthur has consistently demonstrated a commitment to using his expertise for national development.

His contributions have affected areas including electricity access, power generation, energy governance, institutional development, human capital and regional integration.

His work on the Northern Electrification and System Reinforcement Project contributed to expanding electricity access to communities in northern Ghana.

His leadership at Bui contributed to the delivery of 400 MW of additional generation capacity.

His authorship of the Grid Code established an enduring framework for the operation of Ghana’s transmission system.

His leadership helped strengthen key public institutions responsible for Ghana’s energy sector.

His emphasis on Ghanaian expertise contributed to developing a stronger pool of local engineers and energy professionals.

His work across West Africa contributed to regional energy cooperation and development.

These contributions demonstrate that his public service has generated value at multiple levels — from national policy and institutions to infrastructure and individual communities.

Recognition of Distinguished Service

Ing. Amissah-Arthur’s long-standing contribution to Ghana’s energy sector has received significant professional recognition.

In 2025, he was adjudged the recipient of the Lifetime Achievement Award at the Ghana Energy Awards.

The recognition reflected his decades of contribution to the energy sector and his impact on Ghana’s power development.

For the purposes of this nomination, the award is significant not because it is the same recognition being sought here, but because it provides independent evidence of the exceptional standing he has earned through his career.

His record of service, leadership and institutional contribution provides the foundation for his nomination for the Distinguished Public Service and Governance Award.

Legacy and Overall Impact

Ing. Jabesh Amissah-Arthur’s legacy can be measured not simply by the positions he has occupied, but by what remains because of his service.

He has helped create and strengthen institutions.

He has helped establish governance frameworks.

He has helped expand electricity access.

He has helped deliver critical national infrastructure.

He has helped build Ghanaian technical capacity.

He has contributed to regional energy cooperation.

And he continues to serve.

His career demonstrates the highest form of public service: applying knowledge, experience and leadership to solving national challenges and creating systems that continue to deliver value beyond one’s own tenure.

Summary of Impact

• National Development: Contributed significantly to Ghana’s electricity infrastructure and national electrification agenda, helping expand access to communities across the country.

• Public-Sector Leadership: Provided executive and strategic leadership at some of Ghana’s most important energy institutions, including VRA and the Bui Power Authority.

• Governance and Policy: Authored the National Electricity Grid Code, creating an enduring framework for the safe, reliable, transparent and non-discriminatory operation of Ghana’s transmission system.

• Infrastructure Delivery: Led the successful delivery of the 400 MW Bui Hydroelectric Project, one of Ghana’s landmark national infrastructure projects.

• Institutional Strengthening: Contributed to building stronger, more effective public institutions capable of delivering strategic national infrastructure.

• Private-Sector Participation: Through his current role as Operations Chair for the Private Sector Participation Programme, he continues to contribute to effective collaboration between the public and private sectors in Ghana’s energy industry.

• Regional Leadership: Contributed to more than 40 major energy projects across West Africa and held leadership positions supporting regional energy cooperation.

• Human Capital Development: Mentored and empowered Ghanaian engineers and professionals, strengthening the country’s technical and leadership capacity.

• Public-Service Recognition: Was adjudged the 2025 Lifetime Achievement Award recipient at the Ghana Energy Awards, recognising his sustained contribution to Ghana’s energy sector.

• Continuing Service: Despite having completed several major executive assignments, he continues to contribute his experience and expertise to Ghana’s development.

Conclusion

Ing. Jabesh Amissah-Arthur’s career represents more than four decades of distinguished public service, professional excellence and commitment to national development.

His contribution has transcended individual projects and appointments. He has helped build institutions, establish governance frameworks, expand electricity access, deliver strategic infrastructure, develop Ghanaian professionals and strengthen regional energy cooperation.

His leadership at the Volta River Authority and Bui Power Authority demonstrated his ability to manage complex public institutions and deliver projects of national significance. His authorship of the Ghana Grid Code demonstrates his contribution to enduring sector governance. His work on the Northern Electrification and System Reinforcement Project demonstrates his commitment to equitable national development. His current role as Operations Chair for the Private Sector Participation Programme demonstrates that his service to Ghana remains active.

His 2025 Lifetime Achievement Award at the Ghana Energy Awards further confirms the exceptional contribution he has made to the energy sector over the course of his career.

Yet his most important legacy is not the awards or titles he has received. It is the lasting public value created through his service — the infrastructure delivered, the institutions strengthened, the governance systems established, the electricity access expanded and the professionals developed.

Ing. Amissah-Arthur exemplifies the qualities expected of a recipient of the Distinguished Public Service and Governance Award: long-standing service to the nation, integrity in leadership, institutional stewardship, policy contribution, accountability, technical excellence, commitment to national development and a demonstrated ability to create lasting public value.

His is a career defined not merely by achievement, but by service — service that has strengthened Ghana’s institutions, advanced its energy sector and contributed meaningfully to the development of the nation and the wider West African region.

Mr. Benjamin Kwame Dontwi started teaching at Mfantsipim in September 1963. He retired as the Headmaster on 31st August 1997, spanning a period of thirty-four (34) years.

He spent all his working life in the School.

He was appointed Acting Headmaster in 1980 and later confirmed Headmaster. He served in this position for seventeen (17) years thus, being the longest serving teacher and Headmaster of Mfantsipim School.

His first students were in Form Three (3) in 1963, the present Class of MOBA ‘66. He taught Biology and Chemistry and was also a Form Master to Form 3B.

It was during the Chemistry lessons on acids and bases that earned him the popular nickname “CORROSIVE”. At first, he never liked the nickname and would quickly respond ‘who shouted corrosive?’ and the classroom would fall dead silent! As this nickname gained wider popularity throughout the School, he accepted it albeit it grudgingly. He continued to teach this class and also be their Form Master from Form Four (4) to Upper Sixth (U6) in 1968.

Mr Dontwi motivated one of his first students to take to teaching after his University education, at Mfantsipim and by astute mentoring, he encouraged this individual’s teaching career and performance at the School. This former student, Mr C. K. Ashun, later succeeded him as Headmaster of Mfantsipim School in 1997 - a clear lesson in succession planning.

At various times of his teaching career in the School, he taught other notable Headmasters and Assistant headmasters such as Mr Koame Edjah, Mr John Simpson, Mr Manfred Odro, Mr. Bannerman-Mensah and Mr Mr Joseph Blankson.

As a teacher, Mr. Dontwi was thorough, systematic, patient and supported theory with practical demonstrations. He ensured that all assignments were marked and discussed in class. At the Sixth Form, he paid particular attention to practical details especially how to weigh chemicals to prepare solutions for titration and analysis. His teaching of Chemistry influenced many of his students to take this subject as their favourite course. Although a friendly teacher, he maintained discipline by ensuring strict attendance to classes (no frepping), punctuality to class, and strict adherence to laboratory standard operating procedures and submitting class assignments on time.   He rose through the ranks as House master, Senior House master, Assistant Headmaster and finally, Headmaster of the School. In all these positions, he acquitted himself creditably and with distinction.

He assumed office as Headmaster of Mfantsipim School in 1980, a very difficult time in the history of this country, when the exodus of teachers to seek greener pastures outside Ghana-especially to Nigeria, was at its peak. With a depleted staff, Mr. Dontwi had to double as Headmaster and a full time Advance Level Chemistry teacher.

The period was also the revolutionary era of the Provisional National Defence Council (PNDC) with its Workers Defence Councils and People’s Defence Councils. He had to navigate through these difficulties cautiously, diplomatically and tactically. Discipline among students was at its low ebb. He countered this firmly and decisively at times, incurring the displeasure of many.

As a teacher and an administrator, he made time for recreation. He played hockey in his youthful days and was a member of the formidable Cape Coast Hockey Club of the 1970s and ‘80s. As he aged, he stuck to ‘dame’, a game he religiously played every evening when time and circumstances permitted.

As Headmaster he was fair, firm, accommodating and very loyal to Mfantsipim School and the Methodist Church Ghana. He improved relations between the School, the Church, the old boys and parents resulting in these crucial stakeholders, providing more substantial assistance to the school in its hour of need during the difficult periods.

nominee_name: The Rt. Hon. Prof. K.A. Busia (1913-1978) MOBA 1931
justification:
On behalf of Busia Foundation International, I nominate Prof. Kofi Abrefa Busia, one of Mfantsipim's most illustrious sons and Africa's foremost scholar-statesmen, for the Distinguished Alumnus Award for Academics and Research.

A product of Wenchi Primary and Mfantsipim School (1927-1931), where he was an outstanding student, Busia blazed a trail that became a template for the Mfantsipim ideal: Dwen Hwe Kan - to think and to look ahead, a motto he exemplified throughout his career.

After teacher training at Wesley College and and External Degree from the University of London he won a Methodist Synod scholarship and became the first African student admitted to University College Oxford earning a BA (Hons) in 1941. He went on to earn an MA in 1946 and a D.Phil (Oxon) in Social Anthropology in 1947 as one of the first group of students admitted to Nuffield, the newly established Graduate College. His doctoral thesis, still in print after nearly 80 years, remains a foundational text in African studies. In the popular imagination this groundbreaking academic career earned him the moniker “Best University Scholar In Africa”.

Most notably his appointment as Professor and Founding Head of the Department of Sociology at the University College of the Gold Coast, now University of Ghana in 1950 made him arguably the first Professor of Sociology on the continent. From 1960-1962 while simultaneously holding a position at the Institute of Social Studies in the Hague, he also became the Inaugural Professor of African Sociology and Culture at the University of Leiden in the Netherlands.

A scholar of international repute Busia held Fellowships from Fulbright, Phelps Stokes and other notable foundations. As well as Visiting Professorships around the world from India to the United States. His last academic position was as Professor at St. Antony's College, Oxford (1962-1969) a position he gave up on his election as Prime Minister of Ghana.

A Prolific Author and Researcher Busia was the author of seminal works including: A Report on the Social Survey of Sekondi-Takoradi (1950); The Position of the Chief in the Modern Political System of Ashanti (1951); The Challenge of Africa(1962); Purposeful Education for Africa(1964) Urban Churches in Britain,(1966)  and Africa in Search of Democracy (1967). His work as an author laid the foundation for the sociology of Africa and the study of African political systems  In addition, the penultimate book on Urban Churches in Britain made him reportedly, for the first time ever, the first African scholar to do a study of the British, rather than the other way around.

Busia’s work as the founding head of the department of Sociology, where he was responsible as early as 1949 for the appointment of a young J.H. Kwabena Nketia an unquestioned luminary ethnomusicologist who incorporated the study of African Music into Sociology was transformational. Distinguished sociologists who were directly his students or were recruited/trained by him in the early years include Prof. E.V.T. Engmann; Prof. C.K. Brown a later long-time Head of Sociology; Prof. Kodjo Senah another former Head with forty years of service to the department. Busia’s record of influence in other universities around the word is equally as impressive. At their 75th anniversary in 2025 many in the department noted that over decades they had produced "thousands of graduates who have become influential in academia, governance, civil society"  and that lineage started with Busia. Scholars such as Nketia long asserted that it is foundations Busia laid within the Sociology department which became the IAS under Nkrumah; a veracity that has gone largely unacknowledged for three quarters of a century. This is the moment to set the record straight.

Prof. Busia demonstrated that an Mfantsipim education could compete and excel at the highest levels of world scholarship. He opened the door for generations of Ghanaian and African academics to follow. His intellectual rigour, commitment to truth, and belief in education as liberation embody the highest values of Mfantsipim. We humbly request that the School posthumously honours this academic giant who carried the Black, Red and White flag to Oxford and around the world.

67_Fraternity Nomination of Frank Ivan Adama Tackie (FGIP)

Urban and Infrastructure Planner, Chief Executive Officer, The Consortium (CIHSD)

Mfantsipim Old Boy, MOBA '67

Category: Distinguished Business and Entrepreneurship Award

Overview

Mr Frank Ivan Adama Tackie is one of Ghana's most accomplished urban and infrastructure planners, with four decades of professional practice spanning more than 20 countries across Africa, Asia, and the Caribbean. He is the founder and Chief Executive Officer of The Consortium for Innovations in Human Settlements Development (CIHSD), a multi-disciplinary firm of architects, town planners and engineers based in Accra, and its subsidiary, Comptran Engineering. A proud old student of Mfantsipim School (MOBA '67), he has combined a distinguished national and international planning career with sustained, hands-on commitment to the development of his alma mater.

Education and Professional Standing

Mr Tackie holds an MPhil in Housing from the University of Newcastle Upon Tyne, England. He began his career with a six-year assignment at the United Nations Centre for Human Settlements (UN-Habitat) in Nairobi, Kenya, where he worked on building and infrastructure projects across roughly 25 countries in Africa, Asia, and the Caribbean — an early international grounding that shaped the pan-African outlook of his later career.

Recognitions

He is a Fellow of the Ghana Institute of Planners (FGIP) and served as President of the Institute from 2001 to 2008, leading the professional body that has represented Ghana's planning community since 1969 and helping set national standards for planning practice.

Leadership

Since founding The Consortium in October 1989, Mr Tackie has served as CEO for over 35 years, directly managing more than 150 projects across the built environment. His clients have included major multilateral and bilateral development agencies — among them the World Bank, USAID, GTZ (now GIZ), the Agence Française de Développement (AFD), the African Development Bank (ADB), and UN-Habitat — reflecting the international trust placed in his firm's technical leadership.

Impact

At the national level, Mr Tackie has been engaged in preparing simplified Land Use and Infrastructure Plans for 12 secondary cities across Ghana under the World Bank's Urban 3 Project. He was involved in the master planning, infrastructure development, and securing funding and an anchor developer for the Legon City Project. He prepared a master plan to regenerate Sekondi-Takoradi into an Oil City, funded by Tullow Oil. He was also involved in the Multi-Storey Car Park Project for City Car Park Ltd on High Street, Accra, delivered through Comptran Engineering and other road and infrastructure development projects.

At the regional and international level, Mr Tackie's four-decade career — spanning UN-Habitat assignments and CIHSD-led consultancies — has carried Ghanaian planning expertise into urban and human-settlements projects across more than 20 countries in Africa, Asia, and the Caribbean, in partnership with agencies such as the World Bank, USAID, GTZ/GIZ, AFD, ADB, and UN-Habitat. This body of work has included planning, housing and infrastructure engagements across the West and East African sub-regions, including Sierra Leone and Uganda among the countries in which The Consortium has undertaken assignments.

Contributions to Mfantsipim

At a landmark 2008 gathering of Mfantsipim old boys at the Accra National Theatre, Mr Tackie presented the vision and master plan for the School's development, introducing "The Mfantsipim Manifesto: A 10-Year Development Agenda," styled "The Renaissance 1."

The Manifesto rested on three pillars: academic excellence ahead of the pack; leadership qualities of discipline and visible Christian values; and an unparalleled environment built for holistic second-cycle education.

As a professional urban and infrastructure planner, he brought direct technical expertise to the School's long-term physical development—applying a career built on master-planning cities to master-planning his alma mater's campus and facilities.

His first attempt to address these issues came in 1996, when MOBA ’67 sought to develop a master plan as its contribution to the 1997 Speech Day. Although that effort was abandoned due to limited interest and cooperation at the time, the idea was revived in 2006 with the full support of the MOBA’67 Year Group. Frank Tackie then drew on his skills in urban design and infrastructure planning, as well as the multidisciplinary capacity of his consultancy firm, The Consortium, to prepare the Mfantsipim Renaissance Plan for presentation at the 2007 Speech and Prize-Giving Day. Mr Tackie bore the full cost of developing the plan.

The plan, which was launched by MOBA National in 2008, introduced a land-use framework that organised the school into academic, student welfare, teacher welfare, and sports zones; coordinated project selection and funding; encouraged pooled support from sponsoring Year Groups for larger initiatives; and promoted a culture of maintenance.

Mr Tackie’s leadership resulted in the Mfantsipim Old Boys Association (MOBA) appointing him as the Lead for Development Projects at the school. The Renaissance model has largely become the blueprint for MOBA projects. The plan is now due for renewal given the school’s limited land capacity and the need for substantial, coordinated funding.

Mentorship and Social Responsibility

Mr Tackie has mentored many young planners, engineers, and valuers through attachments at his companies. The National Service Scheme also sends young graduates to Mr Tackie’s outfit.

He is a member of the Accra Ridge Church, where he has made his expertise available freely. At one time, he managed the church's properties and actively supported new construction on the church premises.

Mr Tackie is known as a generous individual, giving freely of his time, expertise, and finances to assist individuals and their families, the church, and the community. Among his classmates and the general body of alumni, he always has a pleasant face and is ready to host events at his home.

Conclusion

Mr Frank Ivan Adama Tackie exemplifies the Mfantsipim Man: a planner and builder whose four-decade career has shaped cities and settlements across Ghana and the wider African continent, and who has, in turn, brought that same expertise home to shape the future of Mfantsipim School itself. As the School marks its 150th anniversary, his record of professional distinction, institutional leadership, and personal commitment to his alma mater make him a fitting candidate for recognition.

award_category: Distinguished Alumnus Public Service and Governance
justification:
JUSTICE EDWARD AMOAKO ASANTE

Justice of the Supreme Court of Ghana | Former President, ECOWAS Community Court of Justice | International Jurist | Mfantsipim Alumnus

Justice Edward Amoako Asante is a distinguished Ghanaian jurist whose career of more than three decades has been marked by judicial excellence, institutional leadership, public service and an enduring commitment to the rule of law and protection of human rights.

An alumnus of Mfantsipim School, Cape Coast, where he pursued his GCE Advanced Level studies from 1983 to 1985, Justice Asante continued to the University of Ghana, Legon, obtaining his Bachelor of Laws (LL.B. Hons) in 1989. He subsequently attended the Ghana School of Law and was called to the Ghana Bar in 1991.

Following several years of legal practice, Justice Asante began a distinguished career on the Bench. He was appointed a Circuit Court Judge in 2002 and elevated to the High Court in 2008. In 2013, he became Supervising High Court Judge for the Western Region of Ghana, exercising administrative oversight over thirty-four courts in the Region while also serving as Presiding Judge of High Court 1, Sekondi-Takoradi.

In July 2018, he was appointed as one of five Judges of the Community Court of Justice, ECOWAS, on secondment from the Judicial Service of Ghana. Shortly afterwards, his peers elected him President of the ECOWAS Court of Justice.

His leadership of the regional Court proved exceptional. Justice Asante was subsequently re-elected in 2020 and again in 2022, becoming President of the Court for an unprecedented three consecutive two-year terms from 2018 to 2024. During this period, he provided judicial, administrative and strategic leadership to one of West Africa's principal regional judicial institutions.

In August 2020, Justice Asante was elevated to the Court of Appeal of Ghana, while continuing his international judicial assignment at the ECOWAS Court.

His tenure at the helm of the ECOWAS Court was characterised by significant institutional modernisation. He directed and oversaw the introduction of electronic case management and virtual court proceedings during the COVID-19 pandemic and subsequently spearheaded the development and deployment of the Court's Electronic Case Management System. These initiatives contributed substantially to the digital transformation of the Court and to improving the accessibility and efficiency of regional justice.

Under his leadership, the ECOWAS Court also achieved important international recognition. In 2020, a decision of the Court received Columbia University's Global Freedom of Expression Award for Best Recognized Judicial Decision. He also spearheaded the delivery of twenty decisions during an external court session — a first in the history of the ECOWAS Court.

Justice Asante's contribution to law and justice extends beyond the courtroom. He has participated in high-level judicial dialogues with judges and officials of institutions including the International Court of Justice, International Criminal Court, Court of Justice of the European Union, European Court of Human Rights, African Court on Human and Peoples' Rights and International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea.

His international standing was further recognised with his election in October 2025 as a Member of the Advisory Committee of the United Nations Human Rights Council in Geneva for a three-year term. In that capacity, he contributes to research and policy work on contemporary human-rights issues, including artificial intelligence and good governance, corruption and human rights, plastic pollution, unilateral coercive measures and the human-rights implications of sea-level rise.

Justice Asante has also contributed extensively to legal scholarship and professional discourse, delivering lectures and papers on human rights, freedom of expression, constitutional governance, climate justice, international law, regional integration and the jurisprudence of the ECOWAS Court at institutions and international forums across Africa, Europe and the Americas.

His service has earned him several distinctions, including the African Bar Medal of Merit Award in Leadership, the Award for Excellence in Leadership, Peace and Community Development, recognition as a Grand Fellow of the Institute of Security and Strategic Studies, and a Citation of Merit from the Sefwi Wiawso Traditional Council for his contribution, benevolence and dedication to his community.

In a further milestone in an already distinguished judicial career, Justice Edward Amoako Asante has now been nominated and vetted for appointment as a Justice of the Supreme Court of Ghana, marking his elevation to the highest court of his country.

From his formative years at Mfantsipim School to the highest levels of national and international judicial service, Justice Edward Amoako Asante's journey embodies the ideals of scholarship, integrity, leadership, service and excellence. His contribution to Ghana's judiciary, regional justice within ECOWAS, international human-rights jurisprudence and judicial institutional development represents a distinguished record of service to Ghana, West Africa and the international community.

As Mfantsipim School commemorates 150 years of shaping generations of leaders, Justice Edward Amoako Asante stands as an outstanding example of the School's enduring legacy — a product of Mfantsipim whose professional journey has taken him from the halls of the School to the highest court of Ghana and to the forefront of regional and international justice.

justification:
Dr Ernest Kwamina Yedu Addison, MOBA 79, is nominated for the Distinguished Alumnus Award in Public Service and Governance.

After Legon, Cambridge and McGill, he gave close to three decades to public service. As Director of Research at the Bank of Ghana from 2003 to 2011 he chaired the committee that redenominated the cedi and helped bring Ghana’s first sovereign bond to market in 2007. He co-chaired the committee that steered Ghana to HIPC completion point and debt relief. He had earlier been Chief Economist of the West African Monetary Institute and spent five years at the African Development Bank as Lead Regional Economist for Southern Africa.

He was Governor from April 2017 to March 2025, across two terms. He carried through the financial sector clean-up of 2017 to 2019, leaving a stronger and better supervised banking system, consolidated inflation targeting, and advanced payments and financial inclusion. He chaired Ghana International Bank, GhIPSS, the Ghana Deposit Protection Corporation, the Financial Stability Council and the Committee of Governors of the West African Monetary Zone, and co-chaired the Financial Stability Board’s Regional Consultative Group for Sub-Saharan Africa. He led the Bank through the pandemic and the severest macroeconomic dislocation in a generation without the office losing its standing.

His contemporaries recognised as much: in 2020 the Bank of Ghana was named Central Bank of the Year for innovation and financial technology, Global Markets named him Governor of the Year for Sub-Saharan Africa, and he chaired the Board of Governors of the IMF and World Bank at the Annual Meetings. In December 2024 he was made a Member of the Order of the Star of Ghana, the country’s highest public service award.

He has remained close to the School, chairing Speech Day in 2019 on our year group’s nomination and giving generously over many years.

nominee_name: Rt. Hon. Prof. Kofi Abrefa Busia
award_category: Distinguished Alumnus Public Service and Governance
justification:
On Behalf of Busia Foundation International, I  nominate Prof. Kofi Abrefa Busia, Prime Minister of the Second Republic of Ghana, for the Distinguished Alumnus Award for Government and Public Service.

In the combination of his birth into the Sofoase Yefiri Royal house of Wenchi alongside his training as a student leader at Mfantsipim, lie Busia’s dedication of his entire life to public service and the pursuit of democratic governance in Ghana and Africa. His record of service is unparalleled:

He was selected As one of the first two Ghanaian District Commissioners appointed for the Gold Coast Colony (and one of only the first four, two in Ghana, two in India) he became very early a voice for the people in indigenizing the higher echelons of the civil service. It was from this service he was appointed by the Crown Colony to organize the Social Survey of Sekondi-Takoradi, considered a model of its form for its insights into urban development and transformation..

In 1951, Busia was elected to the Legislative Council by the Ashanti Confederacy and in 1952, formed the Ghana Congress Party of what remained of the UGCC after the split with the CPP. In 1957, after the Avoidance of Discrimination Act, which banned parties based on tribal/regional/religious affiliation, the Northern People's Party, the National Liberation Movement, the Muslim Association Party, the Anlo Youth Organization and Togoland Congress etc. all merged under Busia’s leadership as the United Party, a notable gesture as he was the sole GCP candidate in the Assembly where the Northern People's Party had 15 seats and the NLM 12 at the time. Thus Busia became Leader of the Opposition United Party at the time of Independence in 1957 because it was recognized that he stood for principled opposition and multi-party democracy during the most turbulent periods of our national history. He went  into exile at universities in Holland, Mexico and in England 1959 after the passage of the Preventive Detention Act, and the 1966 Coup d’Etat which overthrew the One Party State.

On returning from his first exile he established the Center for Civic Education to establish just that, the importance of civic education for a well informed independent citizenry. A position from which he argued for the return to civilian rule and an attitude that informed his contributions to the second constituent assembly.

Following the Progress Party’s historic landslide victory in the 1969 elections, he became Prime Minister of the Second Republic of Ghana (1969-1972). As Head of Government he restored the rule of law, freedom of speech, and press freedom. Amongst their many achievements, his government established the first ever Ministry for Social and Rural Development, notable for the extraordinary water projects it succeeded in establishing around the country; his administration was environmentally visionary in establishing the Mole National Park; In the areas of  Education & Labour they expanded primary education in rural areas, and established the National Service Corps; championed decentralization, and pursued a foreign policy of Dialogue with South Africa. This policy, misunderstood (and therefore vilified at the time), is now acknowledged as what in the end, two decades later, brought down the Apartheid regime and led to the election of Nelson Mandela. Busia remains the model of an intellectual in politics - incorruptible, modest, and visionary; qualities which also made him an International Statesman:

He served on numerous international bodies, including the World Council of Churches and the UNESCO Executive, and was a respected advisor on African affairs to world leaders. He consistently demonstrated that democracy was a system intrinsic to African communal values and thus suited to contemporary multi-party state formation.

Busia's life exemplified the Mfantsipim creed of selfless leadership and service to the nation. He lived simply, served honestly, and left office poorer than he entered - a rare testament to integrity in public life. His famous maxim that democracy requires "a market, a forum and a system of justice" continues to guide Ghana's democratic journey.

Though he passed away in exile in Oxford on August 28, 1978, his legacy as a democrat, a patriot, and a servant of Ghana endures. Honouring him is honouring the best of Mfantsipim's contribution to nation-building.

I am pleased to nominate Daniel Fiifi Tawia Hagan, Ph.D. for the Science, Technology and Innovation Award in recognition of his outstanding contributions to hydro-climate science, environmental technology, and the practical application of research to global food and water security.

Dr. Hagan is an accomplished hydro-climate research scientist whose work combines satellite Earth observations, climate modelling, hydrological modelling, data assimilation, and causal inference to address some of the most urgent challenges associated with climate change. His research has produced innovative methods for understanding droughts, floods, heatwaves, soil-moisture dynamics, land-surface temperature, and evapotranspiration. He has also developed high-resolution drought-monitoring data, long-term environmental datasets, improved satellite-retrieval algorithms, and causal-analysis frameworks with applications in both scientific research and operational climate-risk management.

His achievements demonstrate a rare combination of scientific depth, technological innovation, and societal relevance. He has contributed to more than 80 SCI-indexed publications, developed patented algorithms for causality and extreme-climate evaluation, and collaborated with leading institutions including Ghent University, the National Center for Atmospheric Research, NASA-related research networks, the European Space Agency, and international academic partners.

Mr. Kwame Twumasi Sarpong is a distinguished Ghanaian entrepreneur, investor, and business leader with over 30 years of experience in building and managing successful enterprises across the insurance, finance, pension, and security sectors. Renowned for his visionary leadership and commitment to economic empowerment, he has played a significant role in shaping Ghana's business landscape through innovation, job creation, and financial inclusion.

After achieving notable success in the United States with Primerica, where he became the company's only Ghanaian Best Salesperson, he returned to Ghana with a vision to contribute to national development through entrepreneurship. He went on to establish several successful businesses, including First Insurance Company Ltd, Ghana's first pure Term Life Insurance company; First Finance Company, an asset management and investment firm; Prestige Pension Trust; and Westec Security Systems Ghana Ltd, the largest Ghanaian-owned private security company.

Beyond his business achievements, Mr. Sarpong is a passionate advocate for mentorship, training, and financial literacy. Through coaching, public speaking, and leadership development initiatives, he has empowered countless young professionals and aspiring entrepreneurs. His contributions have earned him recognition as an inductee into the Corporate Ghana Hall of Fame and as an Outstanding Personality in the Insurance Industry.

A proud alumnus of Mfantsipim School, Mr. Sarpong remains committed to creating opportunities for others and advancing financial empowerment across Ghana. His vision of creating 250,000 millionaires reflects his belief that wealth creation should be a tool for national transformation. His legacy is defined not only by business success but also by his dedication to developing people, creating jobs, and inspiring future generations of leaders.

Togbi Nyaho Tamakloe VI (formerly Ezekiel Keli Tamakloe) is a distinguished traditional leader, public administrator, governance expert, and community development advocate whose career spans education, local government administration, Indigenous governance, police oversight, and traditional leadership in both Ghana and Canada.

A member of the Mfantsipim School Class of 1980, he holds a Bachelor of Social Science (Sociology) with a Diploma in Education and an MBA. He began his professional career as an educator in Botswana before relocating to Canada, where he pursued graduate studies and became actively involved in student leadership and community service.

Over a career spanning more than three decades, he held several senior executive positions, including Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer of the Atikameg First Nation Reserve in Alberta, Canada, where he played a key role in strengthening Indigenous governance and community development. He also served as the inaugural Chief Financial Officer of the Kee Tas Kee Now Tribal Council, which today represents five First Nations communities.

As Chief Administrative Officer of the Town of High Prairie, he provided executive leadership in municipal governance, financial management, and infrastructure development. He further contributed to public accountability and safety as a Police Commissioner for the City of Edmonton, where he helped oversee governance, operations, finance, and police reform initiatives.

In 2021, he was enstooled as Togbi Nyaho Tamakloe VI, becoming the Paramount Chief and Leader of the Royal Adzovia Clan. Since assuming traditional leadership, he has championed governance reforms, education, healthcare, environmental sustainability, diaspora engagement, and community development within the Anlo Kingdom. Notably, he led the successful establishment of the Kome Shime Traditional Council, serving as its inaugural President.

A strong advocate for Pan-Africanism and diaspora relations, Togbi has fostered cultural and economic links between Africa and people of African descent worldwide. His leadership has earned him numerous national and international awards recognizing his contributions to public service, governance, traditional leadership, and community development.

Throughout his life and career, Togbi Nyaho Tamakloe VI has exemplified the values of leadership, integrity, excellence, and selfless service, dedicating himself to improving communities, strengthening institutions, and empowering future generations both in Ghana and abroad.

Dr. Kwame Dapaah-Afriyie is a distinguished Ghanaian physician, medical educator, researcher, and proud member of the Mfantsipim School Class of 1980. Since qualifying as a medical doctor in 1986 from the School of Medical Sciences, Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), he has built an outstanding international career in clinical medicine, medical education, and academic leadership.

A passionate advocate for medical training and healthcare development, Dr. Dapaah-Afriyie established a Medical Student Exchange Programme at Brown University, providing valuable educational opportunities for medical students from the University of Ghana Medical School and KNUST School of Medical Sciences. For over fifteen years, he has made annual visits to Ghana to teach and examine medical students at KNUST and has also contributed to medical education at the University of Development Studies (UDS) and the University of Health and Allied Sciences (UHAS).

Widely respected as a clinical educator in the United States, he has received numerous teaching awards and serves on the Item-Writing Task Force of the American Board of Internal Medicine, helping to shape standards for physician certification. He is a Fellow of the American College of Physicians, the Royal College of Physicians (London), and the Ghana College of Physicians and Surgeons.

Dr. Dapaah-Afriyie is also a founding editor of the Brown Hospital Medicine Journal, reflecting his commitment to advancing medical scholarship and research. His leadership within the medical profession has been recognized through his appointment as Governor of the Rhode Island Chapter of the American College of Physicians, and he made history as the first Ghanaian to serve on the Executive Committee of the American College of Physicians.

Beyond his professional achievements, he remains deeply committed to Mfantsipim School and MOBA, actively supporting philanthropic initiatives and contributing to the development of future generations of healthcare professionals. His career exemplifies excellence in medicine, education, leadership, and service to humanity.

Prof. Kwesi Aning is a distinguished Ghanaian scholar, educator, administrator, and international policy expert whose career has focused on peacebuilding, security studies, governance, counter-terrorism, and conflict prevention. An alumnus of Mfantsipim School, he earned degrees from the University of Ghana and the University of Copenhagen, where he obtained a PhD in Political Science.

Over the course of his career, Prof. Aning has held several prominent academic and policy positions, including serving as the Founding Director of the Faculty of Academic Affairs and Research (FAAR) at the Kofi Annan International Peacekeeping Training Centre (KAIPTC) for nearly two decades. He also served as the African Union's first Expert on Counter-terrorism and has provided advisory and consultancy services to the United Nations, including contributions to UN Security Council reports, evaluations of global counter-terrorism programmes, and membership on the UN Secretary-General's Advisory Group for the Peacebuilding Fund.

Internationally recognized for his scholarship, Prof. Aning was appointed Claude Ake Professor at the Nordic Africa Institute and Uppsala University in Sweden and has held research appointments at leading institutions in Denmark and South Africa. His research focuses on security studies, peacekeeping, democratic governance, political transitions, organized crime, and African security architecture.

With more than 150 academic publications, including books, journal articles, and book chapters, he is one of Africa's leading voices on peace and security issues. His work has influenced both academic discourse and international policy. In 2023, he received Chatham House's Centenary Prize for his contribution to international relations scholarship, and in 2026 he was ranked among Ghana's top scientists.

Through his scholarship, academic leadership, and policy contributions, Prof. Kwesi Aning has made a significant impact on peace and security studies in Africa and globally, bringing considerable distinction to Ghana and Mfantsipim School.

Professor Derek Asiedu-Akrofi is an accomplished international lawyer, academic, diplomat, and business executive with over thirty years of experience in international law, business, financial fraud, and immigration. Throughout his distinguished career, he has advised governments and corporations across Sub-Saharan Africa, the Caribbean, Asia, and the former Soviet Republics, earning a reputation as a respected expert in international legal and financial affairs.

His career has successfully bridged academia and industry. He has held senior positions including Legal Counsel at the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in Washington, D.C., Course Director at the International Law Institute, and Non-Executive Director of London Petroleum and Chemical PLC in the United Kingdom. In academia, he has taught and conducted research at several prestigious institutions, including Tufts University's Fletcher School of Law and Diplomacy, Boston University School of Law, Loyola Law School, Loyola Marymount University, the University of Warwick, and the University of International Business and Economics in Beijing.

Professor Asiedu-Akrofi has also served in significant diplomatic and advisory roles, including Honorary Consul of Ghana to Los Angeles, Legal Consultant to the United Nations Centre on Transnational Corporations, and consultant on various USAID projects. His expertise has been sought by international organizations and private sector entities across the globe.

Academically, he holds an LL.B. (Hons) from the University of Benin, Nigeria; an LL.M. in International Law from the University of British Columbia, Canada; and both an LL.M. and a Doctorate in International Banking and Monetary Law from Columbia University School of Law in New York.

He currently serves as President and Chief Executive Officer of Akrofi and Akrofi P.L.C. in Los Angeles, where he leads a specialized law firm focused on international law and immigration. His legal practice includes successful representation of clients before U.S. federal and state courts as well as the International Criminal Court in The Hague.

A proud member of MOBA '80, Professor Asiedu-Akrofi exemplifies global excellence, intellectual achievement, and professional leadership. His distinguished career has brought honor to Mfantsipim School and serves as an inspiration to alumni and aspiring professionals around the world.

Rev. Ing. Kofi Atua Ankama-Asamoah is a distinguished alumnus of Mfantsipim School, engineer, minister of the gospel, and long-serving fraternity leader whose unwavering dedication to MOBA and Mfantsipim has spanned more than four decades. He has served as President of MOBA '80 for over 25 years and has been an active member of the MOBA National Council throughout that period, providing visionary leadership and fostering strong bonds among alumni.

His commitment to Mfantsipim began during his university days at KNUST, where as President of MOBA KNUST, he organized teams of alumni to return to Mfantsipim during vacations to serve as volunteer teaching assistants. As President of MOBA '80, he has spearheaded several landmark projects that have significantly enhanced the school's infrastructure and development.

Among his notable achievements are leading the Sponsoring Year Group in delivering the Academic Site Ablution Project in 2010, an innovative sanitation and biogas facility, and overseeing the construction of the Basketball Court and Sports Facilities Project in 2020, a pioneering initiative that expanded support for sports development in the school. Under his leadership, MOBA '80 also undertook extensive classroom renovations, career guidance programmes, and charitable outreach activities in celebration of its 50th anniversary.

Beyond infrastructure development, Rev. Ing. Ankama-Asamoah is renowned for his commitment to alumni welfare. Through initiatives such as Brothers Keepers, he has championed support for less privileged classmates, widows, widowers, and children of deceased year group members through financial assistance, mentorship, visits, and social support. His leadership has fostered a culture of care, solidarity, and lifelong brotherhood within MOBA '80.

A dedicated servant-leader, Rev. Ing. Kofi Ankama-Asamoah has consistently ensured that MOBA '80 remains exemplary in fulfilling its obligations to MOBA National and contributing to the growth and advancement of Mfantsipim School. His legacy is one of selfless service, fraternity, philanthropy, and enduring commitment to the values of Kwabotwe.

Kweku Brebu Andah is a highly accomplished Ghanaian chartered accountant, tax professional, management consultant, and business leader. He serves as the Managing Partner and Country Partner of Baker Tilly Andah + Andah, one of Ghana's leading professional services firms.

He is a Fellow of the Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA), UK, a Fellow of the Institute of Chartered Accountants, Ghana (ICAG), and a Fellow of the Chartered Institute of Taxation. He also holds a Master's degree in Economic Policy Management, an LL.B., and other professional qualifications.

Over the course of his career, Kweku Brebu Andah has accumulated extensive experience in:

Accountancy and auditing

Taxation

Corporate finance

Insolvency and restructuring

Management and development consulting

Research and training

Financial and investment advisory services

His broad consulting background spans both the private and public sectors, giving him a comprehensive understanding of industry, governance, finance, and institutional development. Through Baker Tilly Andah + Andah, he has contributed significantly to professional services, business advisory, and financial management in Ghana.

In summary, Kweku Brebu Andah is one of Ghana's leading accounting and business advisory professionals, recognized for his expertise in auditing, taxation, corporate finance, and management consulting, and for his leadership of Baker Tilly Andah + Andah.

Rev. Dr. Emmanuel Kwabena Ansah is a distinguished Christian leader, governance expert, author, and organizational development practitioner who has devoted his career to promoting ethical leadership, church governance, and institutional excellence in Ghana and beyond.

He serves as the Convenor and Executive Director of Kingdom Equip Network (KEN), a Christian governance organization based in Accra, and is the Deputy General Overseer of Covenant Family Community Church. Ordained into ministry in 1994, he has emerged as one of Ghana's leading voices on church governance, leadership, ethics, and church-state relations.

Beyond ministry, Rev. Dr. Ansah has held several key leadership positions, including Board Chairman of Transparency International Ghana and Prison Fellowship Ghana, while previously serving as a board member of Scripture Union Ghana and General Secretary of the National Association of Charismatic and Christian Churches (NACCC). He also served as Ghana Director of Globethics, a Geneva-based organization dedicated to promoting ethics in higher education.

A respected educator and leadership consultant, he facilitates training and capacity-building programmes in leadership and governance across Africa through partnerships with organizations such as CORAT Africa. He is also a faculty member of Promise Christian University, California, and is a sought-after speaker on leadership, governance, and organizational development.

Rev. Dr. Ansah holds a Doctor of Ministry in Church Planting and Pastoral Management, an MBA, and is a member of the Institute of Directors-Ghana (IoD-Gh). He is also an accomplished author, having written nearly 20 books on leadership, church governance, ethics, succession planning, conflict management, and Christian living.

Through his ministry, writing, leadership training, and governance advocacy, Rev. Dr. Ansah has made significant contributions to strengthening institutions, developing leaders, and promoting integrity and accountability in both church and society. His life and work exemplify service, ethical leadership, and a commitment to nation-building.

Arc. Kofi Essel-Appiah is a highly accomplished Ghanaian architect, educator, and design leader with an international reputation for excellence in architecture, urban planning, and the built environment. After receiving his architectural education at the Federal University of Rio Grande do Sul (UFRGS) in Brazil, he gained professional experience abroad before returning to Ghana to establish his own practice.

He is the Founder and Principal of PREDIOS Group, an architectural firm established in Accra in the mid-1990s that has grown into one of Ghana's leading design practices, delivering projects ranging from urban master plans and civic buildings to educational institutions, hospitality facilities, workplaces, and private developments. His work is recognized for its creativity, strong conceptual foundations, and innovative integration of culture and contemporary design.

Among his notable projects are the Japanese Embassy in Ghana, the University of Ghana Law Faculty Building, the Central University Master Plan, the ICGC Headquarters, and the Golden Tulip Hotel in Kumasi, among several landmark developments across Ghana.

Beyond professional practice, Arc. Essel-Appiah has played a significant leadership role in advancing the architectural profession in Ghana. He serves as Board Chairman of the Architects Registration Council (ARC) and has previously served on the Council of the Ghana Institute of Architects. He is also an Academic Advisor to the African Futures Institute (AFI), contributing to the development of architectural education and research on the continent.

A respected thought leader, he is known for exploring the intersection of architecture, culture, and identity. His work and public lectures have contributed to important discussions about African architectural expression and contemporary design practice.

In summary, Arc. Kofi Essel-Appiah is one of Ghana's foremost architects and built-environment leaders whose contributions to architectural practice, professional development, and design education have significantly shaped Ghana's architectural landscape and enhanced the country's reputation in the field of architecture.

Dr. Emmanuel Arthur is a distinguished marketing academic, educational leader, and Christian minister with over twenty-six years of experience in higher education and a successful corporate career in marketing and communications. A proud member of MOBA ’80, he received his secondary education at Mfantsipim School before pursuing advanced studies in Ghana and the United Kingdom, culminating in a PhD from London Metropolitan University.

His professional career spans both industry and academia. In the corporate sector, he served as the first Marketing Manager of Ghana Airports Company Limited, where he played a key role in the rebranding of Ghana's airports following the separation of the company from the Ghana Civil Aviation Authority.

As an academic, Dr. Arthur has taught Marketing and Business at several tertiary institutions, including Central University and the Ghana Institute of Journalism (now UniMAC). At Central University, he contributed significantly to programme development, student recruitment, and international partnerships, helping to establish an MSc Marketing Research programme and innovative admissions strategies.

Since joining Lancaster University Ghana in 2015, he has risen through the ranks from Lecturer to Head of Business Studies, Provost, and subsequently Chief Executive Officer, becoming the first African and Ghanaian to hold both the Provost and CEO positions at the institution. Under his leadership, student enrolment significantly increased, and Lancaster University Ghana strengthened its reputation as one of Africa's leading British branch campuses.

Beyond academia, Dr. Arthur is an accomplished researcher, journal reviewer, and consultant who has contributed to the advancement of business education and professional practice in Ghana. He is also a devoted Christian leader, having served Action Chapel International for over three decades. Ordained as a Reverend Minister in 2016, he currently serves as Branch Pastor and has been instrumental in church growth, youth mentorship, career guidance, and educational support initiatives.

Dr. Arthur's life reflects a commitment to excellence, leadership, service, education, and faith. Through his achievements in academia, administration, mentorship, and ministry, he exemplifies the values of Mfantsipim School and continues to make a lasting impact on education and society in Ghana.

Henry Kwasi Prempeh-Eck is a distinguished Ghanaian lawyer, legal educator, administrator, mediator, and governance advocate whose career has significantly influenced legal education and professional development in Ghana. A proud alumnus of Mfantsipim School, he was called to the Ghana Bar in 1988 and later earned a Master of Laws (LL.M.) degree from Queen's University in Canada.

He is widely recognized as the longest-serving Director of Legal Education and Director of the Ghana School of Law, where he played a pivotal role in shaping legal education and professional training for generations of Ghanaian lawyers. Prior to becoming Director, he served as a Senior Lecturer at the Ghana School of Law, teaching Practical Conveyancing, Land Law, and Drafting of Deeds and Documents. Before entering academia, he worked in the banking sector, serving as Head of Recoveries at what later became Republic Bank (Ghana).

In private legal practice, Mr. Prempeh-Eck is a Partner at Lex-Eck Consult, providing legal advisory and representation services. He is a member of the Ghana Bar Association, the International Bar Association, and the Commonwealth Lawyers Association, and is also a founding member of the Ghana Association of Certified Mediators and Arbitrators (GHACMA).

Beyond his professional work, he has contributed extensively to governance and public service through his membership on various boards, including the Legal Aid Commission, Ghana Integrity Initiative (Transparency International Ghana), and PIE Ghana, an educational charity that has supported numerous senior high schools and tertiary institutions with laboratory equipment, computers, and educational resources.

Through decades of service to legal education, professional training, mediation, governance, and educational philanthropy, Henry Kwasi Prempeh-Eck has established a legacy of leadership, public service, and commitment to developing Ghana's legal profession and educational sector.

Rt. Rev. Jeremiah Amo Morrison is a distinguished educator, church leader, educational administrator, and proud alumnus of Mfantsipim School whose career has spanned more than four decades of dedicated service to education, faith, and national development.

Born on 26 September 1954, he attended Mfantsipim School from 1967 to 1972 before continuing his studies at Aggrey Memorial Zion Secondary School. He subsequently obtained a Bachelor of Arts (Honours) and Diploma in Education from the University of Cape Coast, a Diploma in Theology from the University of Ghana through Trinity College, Legon, and a Master's Degree from the University of Birmingham in the United Kingdom.

His educational career began in 1981 at Mfantsipim School, where he taught History at both ordinary and advanced levels. During this period, he also taught History part-time at Ghana National College and at the Workers' College of the University of Ghana, Cape Coast Centre. He later served as Chaplain and teacher at Mfantsiman Girls' Secondary School, where he taught Geography, Bible Knowledge, and Religious Studies, contributing significantly to the academic and moral development of students.

From 1991 to 1994, Rt. Rev. Morrison served as Headmaster of Methodist High School, Saltpond, providing educational leadership and strengthening the institution's academic standards and administration. He subsequently joined the University College of Education, Winneba, and later the University of Education, Winneba, where he served in the Registrar's Office as a Senior Member between 1994 and 2000 and again from 2012 to 2016, contributing to the effective administration and growth of tertiary education in Ghana.

Beyond classroom teaching and educational administration, Rt. Rev. Morrison has played an influential role in educational governance and policy. He served as a Member of the Ghana National Commission for UNESCO from 1997 to 2000 and was a Resource Person at the National Forum on Education in 1998. His commitment to education is further demonstrated through his service on numerous Boards of Governors and Boards of Management of leading secondary schools across Ghana. These include serving as Chairman of the Boards of Breman Asikuma Senior High School and Mfantsiman Girls' Senior High School, as well as serving on the boards of Mfantsipim School, Methodist Girls' Senior High School, Mamfe, Juaben SHS, Methodist SHS, Saltpond, and currently Jukwa Senior High Technical School.

One of his notable educational legacies is the founding of St. Paul Methodist Preparatory and Junior High School in Winneba in 1999, an institution established to provide quality educational opportunities for young people.

Alongside his educational achievements, Rt. Rev. Morrison has had a remarkable career in the Methodist Church Ghana, serving as a minister in full connexion from 1981 to 2024. During this period, he held several significant leadership positions, including Synod Secretary of the Cape Coast District, Synod Secretary of the Winneba Diocese, Bishop of the Winneba Diocese, Superintendent Minister in both the Koforidua and Effiduase Dioceses, and Director of Pastoral Care and Counselling of the Methodist Church Ghana. Since 2024, he has served as a Supernumerary Minister, continuing to offer counsel and support to the Church.

Throughout his life and career, Rt. Rev. Morrison has demonstrated an unwavering commitment to academic excellence, character formation, educational leadership, church ministry, and national service. His contributions have impacted thousands of students, educators, clergy, and communities across Ghana. As an educator, administrator, bishop, mentor, and public servant, he embodies the values of leadership, integrity, service, and excellence that Mfantsipim School seeks to instill in its students.

His legacy is one of transformative leadership in both education and ministry, making him an outstanding example of a Mfantsipim alumnus whose life's work has contributed significantly to the development of education, faith, and society in Ghana.

justification:
KODA, born Augustine Kofi Owusu Dua Anto (15 December 1978 – 21 April 2024), was one of Ghana's most influential gospel musicians, songwriters, producers, multi-instrumentalists, and music ministers. Widely respected for his exceptional musical talent and deep spiritual messages, he left a lasting impact on Ghanaian gospel music through both his own recordings and his work behind the scenes as a producer and mentor.

Born in Sekondi-Takoradi, KODA developed a passion for music at an early age after his mother enrolled him in music lessons, where he learned to play the guitar. He later attended the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), where he became Mass Choir Director and played key leadership roles in several music groups, including the Baptist Students Union Music Wing, Simply Jazz Crew, God's Instruments, and the renowned contemporary gospel group Da Project.

KODA first gained prominence as a music producer, working on acclaimed gospel albums for leading artists such as Nii Okai, Danny Nettey, Pastor Joe Beecham, Daughters of Glorious Jesus, Pastor Helen Yawson, Joyful Way Incorporated, Diana Hamilton, and Nathaniel Bassey, among others. His production skills earned him recognition as one of Ghana's finest gospel music producers.

As a recording artist, KODA built a successful music career with several celebrated albums, including Nyame Beye, Waye Wie, Black & White, Oxygen, Hosanna, and Keteke. Many of his songs, such as Nkwaa Abodoo, Nsem Pii, Guide Me O, Adooso, and Yaa Pae, became gospel classics and were admired for their rich musical quality and powerful Christian messages. His music combined worship, contemporary gospel, and jazz influences, creating a unique sound that resonated with diverse audiences.

Beyond performance and recording, KODA was passionate about music education. He produced instructional materials for aspiring musicians and mentored many younger gospel artists. His influence extended beyond Ghana through collaborations with international gospel ministries and musicians. Because of his bold and thought-provoking lyrical content, he became known by many as the"Preacher's Preacher," a title reflecting his ability to address spiritual and social issues through music.

Throughout his career, KODA received several awards and nominations, including recognition for his work as a producer and songwriter. His contributions helped shape contemporary gospel music in Ghana and inspired a generation of worship leaders, producers, and singers.

KODA was married to fellow musician Ewurama Dua Anto, and they had three children. He passed away on 21 April 2024 at the age of 45, leaving behind a rich legacy of music, ministry, mentorship, and creative excellence. His death was widely mourned across Ghana and the international gospel music community.

In summary, KODA was an iconic Ghanaian gospel musician whose extraordinary gifts as a singer, songwriter, producer, instrumentalist, and mentor transformed the gospel music landscape and established him as one of the most respected figures in contemporary African gospel music.

His distinguished career also includes senior leadership of agribusiness enterprises, major national development initiatives and international programmes, complemented by recognition from institutions including GIRSAL, ACDI/VOCA, the African Development Bank and the Government of Ghana.

Beyond his professional achievements, KK has demonstrated exceptional commitment to service, integrity and the Mfantsipim fraternity. As a proud MOBA 1979 alumnus, Freeman Aggrey House member and Chairman of the 1979 Year Group Welfare Committee, he has consistently supported Mfantsipim, including significant contributions to fundraising initiatives. His combination of entrepreneurial achievement, institution-building, national impact, character and enduring service to his School makes him an outstanding and highly deserving candidate for this award.

Emmanuel Mensah Boateng is a worthy nominee for the Distinguished MOBA International Ambassador Award. As a Ghanaian engineering and project-management professional in Germany, he has distinguished himself through international leadership, academic excellence, and sustained service to multicultural communities. In his current work, Emmanuel leads the delivery of complex automotive-validation projects across onshore, nearshore, and offshore teams of more than 60 professionals, with responsibility for an annual budget of approximately €5 million. His career spans research, advanced engineering, and technical project management with leading organisations including Cognizant Mobility, Magna, ZF Friedrichshafen, and the University of Stuttgart.

Equally important is his record of building bridges across cultures. During his studies at Ravensburg-Weingarten University, Emmanuel led the African Students Union and helped organise its annual cultural and sporting events, promoting African visibility, mutual understanding, and inclusion. He also served on the City of Weingarten’s Integration Council. The university recognised his exceptional academic performance and social commitment with the DAAD Prize, noting his leadership, cultural engagement, and contribution to the student community.Through professional excellence, integrity, and service, Emmanuel projects the values of Mfantsipim and Ghana internationally. He is an example to young people: globally capable, rooted in community, and committed to using knowledge and leadership to connect people and create impact.
